references.text: The ephod was part of the high priest's garment used to seek God's will; here, Micah made his own unauthorized ephod.
The description of the official ephod and breastpiece that God commanded Moses to make, in contrast to Micah's unauthorized version.
Rachel stole teraphim (household gods) from her father Laban, the same type of idolatrous objects that Micah made.
Terafim are mentioned again in connection with Rachel, showing that these idolatrous objects were widespread.
The continuation of the story about Micah and his private priest, where he hires a Levite.
The Danites stole Micah's ephod, teraphim, and priest, demonstrating the consequences of his unauthorized worship.
Only Levites were to serve at the sanctuary, but Micah consecrated his own son as priest.
Jeroboam also appointed priests who were not from the tribe of Levi, a similar sin that Micah committed.
The prophet Hosea mentions that Israel will be without ephod and teraphim, showing that these objects were widespread in idol worship.
